# Results — Study 318 (Election-Volatility) on the real tape

*Generated by the engine in [`election_volatility/`](../election_volatility/) on the
shared cached tapes. The volatility/event angle on US presidential elections: (1) does
**realized** vol spike into election day, (2) does **implied** vol (VIX) over-price the
realized vol that follows — a variance-risk premium — and (3) does a short-vol carry
timed to the election pay an edge **over the always-on VRP you'd earn any time**.
Price-only indices: ^GSPC (S&P 500 level, no dividends) for realized vol, ^VIX for
implied vol. As-of **2026-06-12**; match the per-tape fingerprint to confirm you hold the
same tape. This study is the **vol** angle — distinct from the *return-cycle* election
studies 81 (Four-Year-Itch) and 248 (Presidential-Honeymoon).*

## Data stamp

| Tape | Window | Days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| ^GSPC (realized vol) | 1927-12-30 → 2026-06-12 | 24,729 | `530904cd97f3` |
| ^VIX (implied vol) | 1990-01-02 → 2026-06-11 | 9,179 | `c391a7a81017` |

Elections covered: all 25 since 1928 on ^GSPC; the 9 of the VIX era (1992–2024) wherever
implied vol is needed.

## 1 · Does realized vol *spike* into the election?

Per-election ratio of realized vol in the 10 sessions **before** election day to a normal
63-session baseline (ending 21 sessions before the run-up, so it is "normal times"):

| Sample | n | mean ratio | t (vs 1.0) | frac > 1 | placebo pctile |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| All elections (1928–2024) | 25 | **1.05** | **+0.54** | 44% | 66 |
| VIX era (1992–2024) | 9 | 1.21 | +1.05 | 56% | — |

The pre-election realized-vol "spike" is **5% on average and statistically
indistinguishable from 1.0** (t = +0.54), sitting at the 66th percentile of a random-date
placebo — i.e. unremarkable. Fewer than half the elections even show *elevated* vol. The
folk image of markets convulsing into election day is, on realized vol, **not there**.

## 2 · Does implied vol over-price realized — a variance-risk premium?

Implied vol the session before the election vs the annualised realized vol over the next
21 sessions (implied − realized = the premium a vol seller collects), VIX era:

| Election | implied | realized | VRP |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1992 | 16.7 | 7.1 | +9.5 |
| 1996 | 18.0 | 9.3 | +8.8 |
| 2000 (contested) | 24.5 | 24.9 | −0.4 |
| 2004 | 16.3 | 10.9 | +5.4 |
| **2008 (GFC)** | 53.7 | **76.8** | **−23.1** |
| 2012 | 18.4 | 14.7 | +3.7 |
| 2016 | 18.7 | 7.5 | +11.2 |
| 2020 | 37.1 | 15.6 | +21.5 |
| 2024 | 22.0 | 11.6 | +10.3 |

| n | mean VRP | t | win-rate | 95% CI |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 9 | **+5.21** | **+1.28** | 78% | [−2.8, +11.8] |

The premium is **positive 7 elections out of 9** and averages +5.2 vol points — but the
cross-event **t = +1.28 is below the inference bar**, and the 95% CI **straddles zero**.
One election does the damage: **2008**, where election day fell inside the global
financial crisis and realized vol (76.8) blew through implied (53.7) for a −23.1
catastrophe. Drop 2008 and the mean VRP jumps to **+8.76 at t = +3.83** — but that is a
*snooped* removal of the one tail event, exactly the event a vol seller has to survive.

## 3 · Could you trade it? — short-vol carry into the election

Sell vol at the close five sessions before the election, buy it back over the next 21
sessions (P&L in vol points = implied − realized; one execution lag, costs charged once
per round trip in vol points; selling vol is the short leg):

| Variant | n | mean (vol pts) | t | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Election carry, gross | 9 | **+6.15** | **+4.51** | 89% |
| Election carry, net (2 vol-pt cost) | 9 | +4.15 | +3.04 | 89% |

A gross t of +4.51 looks like a slam-dunk — **and it is the trap this study exists to
expose.** Selling vol pays a premium *all the time* (the variance-risk premium), not just
into elections. The honest race is **excess over the always-on carry**: the same trade on
random non-election dates earns **+3.80 vol points** by itself.

| Race | mean (vol pts) | t | placebo basket pctile |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Election carry (gross) | +6.15 | +4.51 | — |
| Always-on carry (random dates) | +3.80 | — | — |
| **Election *excess* over always-on** | **+2.35** | **+1.72** | 88 |

The election-*specific* excess is **+2.35 vol points at t = +1.72** — **below the bar**,
with a 95% CI of **[−0.2, +4.8]** that includes zero, and the 9-election basket sits at
the 88th percentile of random 9-date baskets (inside the bulk, not the tail). Most of the
headline carry is the ordinary VRP you would harvest on any random Tuesday.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful detector

On the deterministic offline tape the machinery recovers a planted election effect **only
when one is planted**, and finds nothing on the null:

| Planted | vol-ratio t (vs 1) | excess-carry t (vs always-on) |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`vol_bump=0, vrp=0`) | +0.93 | +1.93 |
| control (`vol_bump≈0.5–0.8, vrp=8`) | +5.84 | +9.20 |

The null clears nothing (|t| < 2); the planted spike and election-excess VRP are
recovered with large t. A synthetic control is a machinery proof, never market evidence —
it certifies the harness, not the claim.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Realized vol does **not** spike into elections (ratio 1.05, t = +0.54,
  66th placebo pctile). Implied vol *does* tend to over-price it (mean VRP +5.2, positive
  7/9), but the cross-event t = +1.28 is below the bar and the CI straddles zero; the
  election-*specific* carry excess over the ordinary VRP is +2.35 vol pts at t = +1.72,
  CI [−0.2, +4.8]. A real-looking premium that this 9-election tape cannot certify.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The eye-catching gross t = +4.51 is **the always-on VRP**, not
  an election edge: random dates earn +3.80 of the +6.15. The election excess (+2.35) is
  not significant and is bought by accepting the 2008-style tail (−23 vol points in a
  single trade) — picking up pennies in front of the steamroller, with no excess pennies
  for the election timing.
- **An election volatility premium, or just the VRP? — MISATTRIBUTED.** What looks like an
  "election risk premium" is overwhelmingly the variance-risk premium present every day;
  strip it out and the election-specific component does not clear significance.
